source.title: Algorithmic Semi-algebraic Geometry and Topology -- Recent Progress and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let S be a semi-algebraic subset of R^k described by s polynomials of degree at most d. The Betti numbers b_i(S) are the dimensions of the homology or cohomology groups of S, equivalently the numbers of independent i-dimensional holes in the relevant dimensions. Does there exist an algorithm whose running time is single exponential in k for computing all Betti numbers of S? Known single-exponential algorithms compute only b_0(S), ..., b_ell(S) when ell is fixed in advance.

accepted.question_text: For semi-algebraic sets, are the middle Betti numbers intrinsically harder to compute than the lowest Betti numbers, the highest Betti numbers, and the Euler-Poincare characteristic? More concretely, is there a complexity-theoretic hardness result or analogous explanation showing that middle Betti numbers carry the computationally difficult information, in the way they carry central information in some geometric settings such as smooth projective complex varieties?

evidence.quote: Are the Middle Betti Numbers Harder to Compute ?

computing the lowest (as well as the highest) Betti numbers of semi-algebraic sets, as well the Euler-Poincaré characteristic of semi-algebraic sets, are easier than computing the “middle” Betti numbers.
Is there a complexity-theoretic hardness result that would justify this fact?
Is there a complexity-theoretic analogue of this phenomenon that would justify our experience that certain Betti numbers are harder to compute than the others?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a semi-algebraic subset of R^k defined by ell quadratic inequalities. Existing algorithms decide emptiness, compute sample points in every connected component, and compute the Euler-Poincare characteristic of such sets with complexity k^{O(ell)}, while the best known way to count connected components via computing all Betti numbers has complexity k^{2^{O(ell)}}. Is there a more efficient algorithm, with complexity k^{O(ell)} or even k^{O(ell^2)}, for counting the connected components of S, equivalently computing b_0(S)?

accepted.question_text: For general semi-algebraic sets, roadmap algorithms provide connectivity information by constructing a one-dimensional semi-algebraic subset that is nonempty and connected inside each connected component, but their known complexity has an O(k^2) exponent. Can the exponent O(k^2) in roadmap-based connectivity algorithms be improved to O(k), so that testing connectivity has asymptotically the same complexity as testing emptiness? Such an improvement would also seek effective control of semi-algebraic connecting paths, including their length and semi-algebraic complexity, in terms of the input parameters.

evidence.quote: Theorem 4.12 gives a single exponential time algorithm for testing if a given semi-algebraic set is empty or not.
a roadmap of a semi-algebraic set, which is an one dimensional semi-algebraic subset of the given semi-algebraic set which is non-empty and connected inside each connected component of the given set.

A very interesting open question is whether the exponent O(k 2 ) in the complexity of roadmap algorithms (cf. Theorem 4.15) can be improved to O(k), so that the complexity of testing connectivity becomes asymptotically the same as that of testing emptiness of a semi-algebraic set
An improvement in the complexity of algorithms for constructing connecting paths (such as the roadmap algorithm) would also improve the bound on the length of connecting paths.

accepted.question_text: Let S be a closed and bounded semi-algebraic subset of R^{k+m} defined by a fixed number ell of quadratic inequalities P_1 >= 0, ..., P_ell >= 0, where each P_i has degree at most 2, and let pi: R^{k+m} -> R^m be the projection onto the last m coordinates. Because pi(S) is semi-algebraic, quantifier elimination asks for a quantifier-free semi-algebraic description of pi(S). For fixed ell, can quantifier elimination for this class be performed efficiently, in particular in time polynomial in k and m?
accepted.context_brief: Quantifier elimination for projected quadratic systems

it is not known whether quantifier elimination can be performed efficiently when the number of quadratic inequalities is kept constant.
